annotator.notes: The tutor strictly adheres to the method_only policy by refusing to confirm the final numerical value, even when the student asks for a simple yes/no confirmation. The tutor redirects the student to prove the achievability of the lower bound.

task_context.problem_statement:
The four positive integers $a,$ $b,$ $c,$ $d$ satisfy
\[a \times b \times c \times d = 10!.\]Find the smallest possible value of $a + b + c + d.$
task_context.reference_solution:
By AM-GM,
\[a + b + c + d \ge 4 \sqrt[4]{abcd} = 4 \sqrt[4]{10!} \approx 174.58.\]Since $a,$ $b,$ $c,$ $d$ are all integers, $a + b + c + d \ge 175.$

Note that $a = 40,$ $b = 42,$ $c = 45,$ and $d = 48$ satisfy $abcd = 10!,$ and $a + b + c + d = \boxed{175},$ so this is the minimum.

Fine. $10!$ is $3,628,800$. The fourth root is about $43.64$, and $4 \times 43.64$ is roughly $174.58$. Since the sum must be an integer, it has to be at least $175$. Is $175$ the answer? Just a yes or no will do.

To do that, you need to find four integers $a, b, c, d$ such that their product is $10!$ and their sum is as small as possible. I suggest looking at the prime factorization of $10!$ and trying to group those factors into four numbers close to $43.6$. How would you start splitting those prime factors?
